boundaries.contract: `cmd_Protocol` is a `ConfCmdFn` stored as `SslConfCmdTbl.cmd` by the private `commands()` table (`src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:990`, row `:1066`). The only indirect invocation is `f(cctx, value)` in `SSL_CONF_cmd` (`:1473`), reached from `SSL_CONF_cmd_argv` (`:1560` -> `:1616`). `SSL_CONF_cmd_value_type` (`:1643`) reads only `value_type`, never `.cmd`. Preconditions: (1) `cctx` is non-NULL, aligned, live, initialised, and exclusively accessible: `SSL_CONF_cmd` rejects a NULL `cctx`/`cmd` at `:1522`; provenance is one zeroed `size_of::<SslConfCtx>()` block from `SSL_CONF_CTX_new` (`:1672`); `SSL_CONF_CTX_set_ssl`/`_set_ssl_ctx` (`:1795`/`:1839`) set `ctx`/`ssl` to NULL or live in-crate objects; the shared `&*cctx` at `:1457` is used only for lookup and ends (NLL) before `:1473`, so the handler's writes do not alias a live shared borrow. (2) `value` is non-NULL and NUL-terminated: `SSL_CONF_cmd` rejects NULL for a typed row at `:1490`; NUL-termination is the public caller contract at `:1489`. (3) No retention of `value`: the handler passes it to `parse_option_list`, which stores only the frame-local flag table in `cctx.tbl` and clears `tbl`/`ntbl` before returning (`:566-567`). (4) Return: `CONF_parse_list` gives 1 when an element matched and 0 otherwise; `SSL_CONF_cmd` maps >0 to 2 and every other value to 0. (5) NULL `cctx` is never delivered (dispatch guard); if it were, the handler would dereference it. A NULL `value` is not delivered either; the handler would answer 0 (CONF_parse_list's NULL arm). (6) Error path: `cctx.tbl`/`ntbl` are cleared on every path; `CONF_parse_list` has its own `guard_ffi`. The slot is private; exclusivity is now a stated precondition of the public SSL_CONF_cmd (# Safety :1489, B46-D1), whose authority documentation states neither (see preconditions).

negative_control.name: ssl::ssl_conf::tests::conf_cmd_dispatch_feeds_a_live_ctx_and_does_not_retain_the_value
negative_control.observation: SSL_CONF_cmd('Options','Bugs') returns 2, sets SSL_OP_ALL in the live option word, and clears cctx.tbl; a second call with '-Bugs' independently clears the bit; a NULL value is refused with -3 and changes no state; a direct cmd_Options(NULL) returns -3. Together these show the callback receives a live SslConfCtx and a NUL-terminated value through the .cmd slot, retains neither, and that a NULL value is handled.

negative_control.limits: The test does not exercise a real SSL/SSL_CTX for every handler; the cipher/protocol handlers are covered only through the shared dispatch/table-clearing path and their static contracts. It does not prove NUL-termination of an arbitrary caller buffer (that is the caller's contract), only that the handler consumes the literal up to its terminator.

negative_control_guard.observation: C4 marks the context in use through the same `enter_use` acquisition the public dispatch performs, shows the re-entrant SSL_CONF_cmd returns 0 with no state change, then shows the context usable again after the guard drops. C5 shows the guard is cleared after the -2 (unrecognised command), -3 (NULL value) and handler-error exits and that the context still works. C6 shows two ordinary sequential calls both succeed and the flag is clear between them.
negative_control_guard.fails_if: SSL_CONF_cmd's `enter_use` acquisition is removed: observed left 2 / right 0 at src/ssl/ssl_conf.rs:2181 (see evidence.mutation).
negative_control_guard.limits: A handler in this slice does not itself call back into SSL_CONF_cmd, so C4 presents the in-flight state through the same guard rather than executing a production handler callback. The guard covers same-thread overlap of SSL_CONF_cmd/SSL_CONF_cmd_argv only; it does not make the wrapped SSL/SSL_CTX safe for cross-thread mutation, and it is not a thread-safety claim.

new_unsafe_assumptions_note: One new production unsafe boundary: `enter_use` takes a raw context address with `addr_of!`, and `InUseGuard::drop` dereferences the stored `*const AtomicBool` to clear the flag. Its contract is that the context is live, aligned and outlives the guard, and that the guard is confined to one public dispatch that holds exclusive access. No signature, exported symbol or `#[repr(C)]` layout changed; the type is opaque and not `repr(C)`.
boundary_size: Seven `unsafe extern "C"` handler bodies in one file, all reached through one private Option<ConfCmdFn> slot. The runtime boundary is the single dispatch edge (ssl_conf_cmd_inner -> f(cctx, value)) plus the five callees (parse_option_list, the four cipher setters, min_max_proto). The B46-D2 guard adds a two-operation internal unsafe abstraction (`addr_of!` + atomic swap/deref in `enter_use`/`InUseGuard::drop`), not a new C-visible symbol. The three new tests add test-only unsafe blocks.
safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: The slots and table are private and the handlers are not exported, so no safe-Rust caller can install a ConfCmdFn. The exported SSL_CONF_cmd is `unsafe extern "C"`; a C caller must satisfy its ':1489' contract (live cctx, NUL-terminated strings). Within the crate all callers are unsafe contexts that satisfy the dispatch guard. The in-use guard is internal and cannot be used by a safe caller to construct a reference.
